subject: Fitting a model with a latent variable

messages.author: c648f9e341bb874c
messages.subject: Fitting a model with a latent variable
parts:
Hello all,

I'm having some difficulty in achieving well-fitting estimates for the parameters in a model containing a observed covariates in addition to a latent covariate. I've pasted the R code and the RStan code used in generating and attempting to fit the model.

Is there an obvious problem with this approach? Perhaps the model is not well-posed (underconstrained/identifiability issues). If so, how can the issues be addressed?

Thanks!


# R code for generating model:

library(rstan)
library(boot)

set.seed(2002)

N <- 1000
M <- 200
K <- 2
J <- 3

X_train <- matrix( rnorm((N*K),0,5), nrow=N )
X_latent_train <- matrix( sample(c(1,0), size=(N*J), replace=TRUE, prob=c(0.45,0.55)), nrow=N )

X_test <- matrix( rnorm((M*K),0,5), nrow=M )
X_latent_test <- matrix( sample(c(1,0), size=(M*J), replace=TRUE, prob=c(0.45,0.55)), nrow=M )

alpha0 <- 2.8
eta <- c(1.2,3.4,1.3)

mu <- alpha0 + X_latent_train%*%eta
sigma <- 2.23
Z <- rnorm(mu, sigma)

alpha1 <- -5
beta <- c(1.3,2.3)
gamma <- 1.5

linear_predictor <- alpha1 + X_train%*%beta + Z*gamma
y <- rbinom( N, 1, inv.logit(linear_predictor) )

model <- stan( file="latent.stan",
data=list(N=N,M=M,K=K,J=J,y=y,X_train=X_train,X_latent_train=X_latent_train,X_test=X_test,X_latent_test=X_latent_test),
pars=c("alpha0","eta","sigma","alpha1","beta","gamma","Z") )


/*
* Latent model: latent.stan
*/

data {

 int N; // # of training cases.
 int M; // # of test cases.
 int K; // # of observed variables.
 int J; // # of variables used in generating latent variable.

 int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N]; // Response vector.
 matrix[N,K] X_train; // Training observed matrix.
 matrix[N,J] X_latent_train; // Training latent matrix.
 matrix[M,K] X_test; // Testing observed matrix.
 matrix[M,J] X_latent_test; // Testing latent matrix.

}

parameters {

 real alpha0;
 vector[J] eta;

 real<lower=0> sigma;

 vector[N] Z; // Latent variable.

 real alpha1;
 vector[K] beta;

 real gamma;

}

transformed parameters {

 vector[N] mu;
 vector[N] linear_predictor;

 mu = alpha0 + X_latent_train*eta;
 linear_predictor = alpha1 + X_train*beta + Z*gamma;

}

model {

 alpha0 ~ normal(0,10);
 for(i in 1:J)
  eta[i] ~ normal(0,10);

 sigma ~ normal(0,10);
 for (n in 1:N)
  Z[n] ~ normal(mu[n], sigma);

 alpha1 ~ normal(0,10);
 for(i in 1:K)
  beta[i] ~ normal(0,10);

 gamma ~ normal(0,10);

 for (n in 1:N)
  y[n] ~ bernoulli_logit(linear_predictor[n]);

}

generated quantities {

 vector[M] y_prediction;
 y_prediction = alpha1 + X_test*beta + (alpha0 + X_latent_test*eta)*gamma; // Results predicted by the model.

}
